162	# ── Model download helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
163	
164	def _download_file(url: str, dest: Path) -> None:
165	    _info(f"Downloading from:\n  {url}")
166	    _info("This may take a few minutes…")
167	
168	    def _progress(block: int, block_size: int, total: int) -> None:
169	        if total > 0:
170	            pct = min(100, block * block_size * 100 // total)
171	            sys.stdout.write(f"\r  {pct}%")
172	            sys.stdout.flush()
173	
174	    try:
175	        urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, dest, reporthook=_progress)
176	    except Exception as exc:
177	        _error(f"Download failed: {exc}")
178	    print()
179	
180	
181	def _safe_tar_members(tf: tarfile.TarFile, dest_dir: Path):
182	    """Yield only safe members, preventing path traversal."""
183	    dest_resolved = dest_dir.resolve()
184	    for member in tf.getmembers():
185	        if member.isdev():
186	            continue
187	        member_path = (dest_dir / member.name).resolve()
188	        try:
189	            member_path.relative_to(dest_resolved)
190	        except ValueError:
191	            continue
192	        yield member
193	
194	
195	def _ensure_model(lang: str, model_dir: Optional[Path], project_dir: Path) -> Path:
196	    """Return the resolved TTS model directory, downloading if needed."""
197	    if lang not in _TTS_MODELS:
198	        _error(
199	            f"Unsupported language '{lang}'. Supported: {list(_TTS_MODELS.keys())}"
200	        )
201	
202	    meta = _TTS_MODELS[lang]
203	    if model_dir is not None:
204	        if not model_dir.is_dir():
205	            _error(f"Model directory not found: {model_dir}")
206	        return model_dir
207	
208	    models_root = project_dir / "models"
209	    target_dir = models_root / meta["extracted"]
210	
211	    if target_dir.is_dir():
212	        return target_dir
213	
214	    # Download and extract
215	    models_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
216	    archive = models_root / meta["archive"]
217	    _info(f"TTS model for '{lang}' not found.")
218	    _download_file(meta["url"], archive)
219	
220	    _info("Extracting…")
221	    try:
222	        with tarfile.open(archive, "r:bz2") as tf:
223	            if sys.version_info >= (3, 12):
224	                tf.extractall(models_root, filter="data")
225	            else:
226	                tf.extractall(models_root, members=_safe_tar_members(tf, models_root))
227	    except Exception as exc:
228	        _error(f"Extraction failed: {exc}")
229	
230	    archive.unlink(missing_ok=True)
231	
232	    if not target_dir.is_dir():
233	        _error(f"Expected model directory not found after extraction: {target_dir}")
234	
235	    _info(f"Model saved to '{target_dir}'.\n")
236	    return target_dir
237	
238	
239	# ── TTS engine ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
240	
241	def build_tts(cfg: TtsConfig, project_dir: Path):
242	    """Build a sherpa_onnx.OfflineTts from *cfg*, downloading the model if needed."""
243	    import sherpa_onnx  # noqa: PLC0415
244	
245	    lang = cfg.language
246	    if lang not in _TTS_MODELS:
247	        _error(
248	            f"Unsupported language '{lang}'. Supported: {list(_TTS_MODELS.keys())}"
249	        )
250	
251	    meta = _TTS_MODELS[lang]
252	    model_dir_override = Path(cfg.model_dir) if cfg.model_dir else None
253	    model_dir = _ensure_model(lang, model_dir_override, project_dir)
254	
255	    config = sherpa_onnx.OfflineTtsConfig(
256	        model=sherpa_onnx.OfflineTtsModelConfig(
257	            vits=sherpa_onnx.OfflineTtsVitsModelConfig(
258	                model=str(model_dir / meta["model"]),
259	                lexicon="",
260	                data_dir=str(model_dir / meta["data_dir"]),
261	                tokens=str(model_dir / meta["tokens"]),
262	            ),
263	            num_threads=cfg.num_threads,
264	        ),
265	    )
266	
267	    if not config.validate():
268	        _error(
269	            "TTS config is invalid — check that all model files exist and are valid."
270	        )
271	
272	    return sherpa_onnx.OfflineTts(config)
273	
274	
275	def synthesise(tts, text: str, cfg: TtsConfig) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:
276	    """Synthesise *text* and return (samples, sample_rate)."""
277	    audio = tts.generate(text=text, sid=cfg.speaker_id, speed=cfg.speed)
278	    samples = np.array(audio.samples, dtype=np.float32)
279	    return samples, audio.sample_rate
280	
281	
282	def _play(samples: np.ndarray, sample_rate: int) -> None:
283	    try:
284	        import sounddevice as sd  # noqa: PLC0415
285	    except ImportError:
286	        _error(
287	            "sounddevice is required for --play. "
288	            "Install it with: pip install sounddevice"
289	        )
290	    sd.play(samples, samplerate=sample_rate)
291	    sd.wait()
292	
293	
294	# ── CLI entry point ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
295	
296	def main() -> None:
297	    args = parse_args()
298	    _validate_runtime_args(args)
299	
300	    project_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
301	
302	    # Resolve text input
303	    if args.text:
304	        text = args.text
305	    elif args.file:
306	        p = Path(args.file)
307	        if not p.exists():
308	            _error(f"Input file not found: {args.file}")
309	        text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
310	    else:
311	        if sys.stdin.isatty():
312	            _console.print("[dim]Reading text from stdin (Ctrl+D to finish)…[/dim]")
313	        text = sys.stdin.read().strip()
314	
315	    if not text:
316	        _error("No text provided. Use --text, --file, or pipe text via stdin.")
317	
318	    model_dir_arg = Path(args.model_dir) if args.model_dir else None
319	    cfg = TtsConfig(
320	        model_dir=str(model_dir_arg) if model_dir_arg else "",
321	        language=args.lang,
322	        speaker_id=args.speaker_id,
323	        speed=args.speed,
324	        output=args.output,
325	        play=args.play,
326	        num_threads=args.threads,
327	    )
328	
329	    _info(f"Language: {cfg.language}  |  speed: {cfg.speed}  |  speaker: {cfg.speaker_id}")
330	    _info("Loading TTS model…")
331	    tts = build_tts(cfg, project_dir)
332	    _info("Synthesising…")
333	
334	    samples, sample_rate = synthesise(tts, text, cfg)
335	
336	    if cfg.play:
337	        _info("Playing audio…")
338	        _play(samples, sample_rate)
339	
340	    sf = _require_soundfile()
341	    sf.write(cfg.output, samples, samplerate=sample_rate)
342	    _info(f"Saved → {cfg.output}")
343	
344	
345	if __name__ == "__main__":

import sherox.segment as seg_module
from sherox.config import SegmentConfig

class TestParseArgs:
    def test_mic_mode(self):
        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.segment", "--mic"]):
            args = seg_module.parse_args()
        assert args.mic is True
        assert args.wav is None

        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.segment", "--wav", "audio.wav"]):
            args = seg_module.parse_args()
        assert args.wav == "audio.wav"
        assert args.mic is False

        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.segment", "--mic", "--wav", "x.wav"]):
            with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
                seg_module.parse_args()

        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.segment"]):
            with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
                seg_module.parse_args()

        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.segment", "--mic"]):
            args = seg_module.parse_args()
        assert args.vad_type == "silero"

        assert args.min_silence == 0.5
        assert args.min_speech == 0.25
        assert args.sample_rate == 16000
        assert args.capture_rate == 16000

class TestValidateRuntimeArgs:

            sample_rate=16000, capture_rate=16000, threads=4,
        )
        defaults.update(kwargs)
        return argparse.Namespace(**defaults)

    def test_threshold_at_boundaries_passes(self):

        seg_module._validate_runtime_args(self._args(threshold=1.0))

    def test_negative_min_silence_exits(self):

    def test_negative_min_speech_exits(self):
        with pytest.raises(SystemExit):

    def test_zero_sample_rate_exits(self):
        with pytest.raises(SystemExit):

    def test_zero_capture_rate_exits(self):
        with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
            seg_module._validate_runtime_args(self._args(capture_rate=0))

    def test_zero_threads_exits(self):

def _make_seg(samples, start=0):
    seg = MagicMock()
    seg.samples = np.array(samples, dtype=np.float32).tolist()
    seg.start = start
    return seg


class TestRunSegment:
    def test_processes_speech_segment(self, capsys):
        vad = MagicMock()
        seg = _make_seg(np.ones(8000), start=0)
        vad.front = seg
        vad.empty.side_effect = [False, True, True]
        cfg = SegmentConfig()
        seg_module.run_segment(vad, iter([np.zeros(1600, dtype="float32")]), cfg, 16000)
        assert "00:" in capsys.readouterr().out

    def test_vad_accept_waveform_called_per_chunk(self):
        vad = MagicMock()
        vad.empty.return_value = True
        cfg = SegmentConfig()
        chunks = [np.zeros(1600, dtype="float32")] * 3
        seg_module.run_segment(vad, iter(chunks), cfg, 16000)
        assert vad.accept_waveform.call_count == 3

    def test_saves_wav_when_output_dir(self, tmp_path):
        vad = MagicMock()
        seg = _make_seg(np.ones(8000), start=0)
        vad.front = seg
        vad.empty.side_effect = [False, True, True]
        cfg = SegmentConfig()
        mock_sf = MagicMock()
        counter = [0]

            seg_module.run_segment(
                vad, iter([np.zeros(1600, dtype="float32")]),
                cfg, 16000, output_dir=tmp_path, segment_counter=counter,
            )
        mock_sf.write.assert_called_once()
        written_path = mock_sf.write.call_args[0][0]
        assert "segment_0000.wav" in written_path
        assert counter[0] == 1

        def interrupt_gen():

class TestParseArgs:
    def test_text_mode(self):
        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.tts", "--text", "Hello"]):
            args = tts_module.parse_args()
        assert args.text == "Hello"
        assert args.file is None

    def test_file_mode(self):
        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.tts", "--file", "input.txt"]):
            args = tts_module.parse_args()
        assert args.file == "input.txt"
        assert args.text is None

    def test_no_text_source_allowed(self):
        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.tts"]):
            args = tts_module.parse_args()
        assert args.text is None
        assert args.file is None

    def test_text_and_file_mutually_exclusive(self):
        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.tts", "--text", "hi", "--file", "f.txt"]):
            with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
                tts_module.parse_args()

    def test_defaults(self):
        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.tts"]):
            args = tts_module.parse_args()
        assert args.lang == "ind"
        assert args.model_dir is None
        assert args.speaker_id == 0
        assert args.speed == 1.0
        assert args.output == "output.wav"
        assert args.play is False
        assert args.threads == 4

    def test_custom_lang(self):
        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.tts", "--lang", "ind"]):
            args = tts_module.parse_args()
        assert args.lang == "ind"

    def test_custom_speed(self):
        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.tts", "--speed", "0.8"]):
            args = tts_module.parse_args()
        assert args.speed == 0.8

    def test_play_flag(self):
        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.tts", "--play"]):
            args = tts_module.parse_args()
        assert args.play is True

    def test_custom_output(self):
        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.tts", "--output", "out.wav"]):
            args = tts_module.parse_args()
        assert args.output == "out.wav"

    def test_custom_threads(self):
        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.tts", "--threads", "8"]):
            args = tts_module.parse_args()
        assert args.threads == 8

    def test_custom_model_dir(self):
        with patch("sys.argv", ["sherox.tts", "--model-dir", "models/custom"]):
            args = tts_module.parse_args()
        assert args.model_dir == "models/custom"

            called["ok"] = True
        with patch("urllib.request.urlretrieve", side_effect=fake_retrieve):
            tts_module._download_file("http://example.com/model.tar.bz2", dest)
        assert called.get("ok")

    def test_progress_skipped_when_total_zero(self, tmp_path):
        dest = tmp_path / "model.tar.bz2"
        def fake_retrieve(url, dest, reporthook):
            reporthook(1, 1024, 0)
        with patch("urllib.request.urlretrieve", side_effect=fake_retrieve):
            tts_module._download_file("http://example.com/model.tar.bz2", dest)

18	def _is_dark_terminal() -> bool:
19	    """Detect whether the terminal has a dark background.
20	
21	    Primary signal: the COLORFGBG environment variable (set by many
22	    xterm-compatible terminals). Its format is ``foreground;background`` where
23	    the background field is a standard ANSI colour index:
24	
25	    +---------+-------------------------------------------+-----------+
26	    | Index   | Colour                                    | BG type   |
27	    +=========+===========================================+===========+
28	    | 0–6     | black, red, green, yellow, blue,          | dark      |
29	    |         | magenta, cyan                             |           |
30	    +---------+-------------------------------------------+-----------+
31	    | 7       | white / light-grey                        | light     |
32	    +---------+-------------------------------------------+-----------+
33	    | 8–15    | bright variants (bright-black … white)    | light     |
34	    +---------+-------------------------------------------+-----------+
35	
36	    Falls back to ``True`` (dark) when the signal is absent — dark backgrounds
37	    are the common default in developer environments.
38	    """
39	    colorfgbg = os.environ.get("COLORFGBG", "")
40	    if colorfgbg:
41	        try:
42	            bg = int(colorfgbg.split(";")[-1])
43	            # Indices 0-6: standard dark colours (black … cyan) → dark bg.
44	            # Index 7 (white) and 8-15 (bright variants) → treat as light.
45	            return bg <= 6
46	        except (ValueError, IndexError):
47	            pass
48	    return True  # Safe default: most developer terminals use a dark background.
49

70	    "dark_green",
71	    "blue",

114	def _dominant_speaker(result: sherpa_onnx.OfflineSpeakerDiarizationResult) -> int:
115	    """Return the speaker id that covers the most time in this segment."""
116	    segments = result.sort_by_start_time()
117	    if not segments:
118	        return 0
119	    duration: dict[int, float] = {}
120	    for seg in segments:
121	        duration[seg.speaker] = duration.get(seg.speaker, 0.0) + (seg.end - seg.start)
122	    return max(duration, key=duration.__getitem__)

247	def run_offline_vad_streaming(
248	    recognizer: sherpa_onnx.OfflineRecognizer,
249	    vad: sherpa_onnx.VoiceActivityDetector,
250	    audio_gen: Generator[np.ndarray, None, None],
251	    sample_rate: int = 48000,
252	    show_mic_level: bool = False,
253	    diarization: Optional[sherpa_onnx.OfflineSpeakerDiarization] = None,
254	    show_speaker_tag: bool = False,
255	) -> None:
256	    """VAD-segmented offline ASR with optional concurrent speaker diarization.
257	
258	    For each speech segment the ASR and diarization models run concurrently
259	    in a ThreadPoolExecutor so that neither doubles the per-segment latency.
260	    Each speaker's output is colour-coded; when *show_speaker_tag* is ``True``
261	    a ``[Speaker N]`` prefix is also printed.
262	    """
263	    executor: Optional[ThreadPoolExecutor] = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) if diarization else None
264	
265	    try:
266	        for chunk in audio_gen:
267	            vad.accept_waveform(chunk)
268	
269	            if show_mic_level:
270	                energy = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(chunk ** 2)))
271	                bar = "█" * min(int(energy * 500), 40)
272	                sys.stdout.write(f"\r{_PREFIX}mic: {bar:<40} {energy:.4f}")
273	                sys.stdout.flush()
274	
275	            while not vad.empty():
276	                segment = vad.front
277	                samples = np.array(segment.samples, dtype=np.float32)
278	                vad.pop()
279	                _decode_and_print(recognizer, samples, sample_rate, diarization, executor, show_speaker_tag)
280	
281	    except KeyboardInterrupt:
282	        pass
283	    finally:
284	        vad.flush()
285	        while not vad.empty():
286	            segment = vad.front
287	            samples = np.array(segment.samples, dtype=np.float32)
288	            vad.pop()
289	            _decode_and_print(recognizer, samples, sample_rate, diarization, executor, show_speaker_tag)
290	        sys.stdout.write("\n")
291	        sys.stdout.flush()
292	        if executor is not None:
293	            executor.shutdown(wait=True)
294	
295	
296	def _decode_and_print(
297	    recognizer: sherpa_onnx.OfflineRecognizer,
298	    samples: np.ndarray,
299	    sample_rate: int,
300	    diarization: Optional[sherpa_onnx.OfflineSpeakerDiarization] = None,
301	    executor: Optional[ThreadPoolExecutor] = None,
302	    show_speaker_tag: bool = False,
303	) -> None:
304	    """Run ASR (and optionally diarization) on *samples* and print the result.
305	
306	    ASR and diarization are submitted concurrently to *executor* so that the
307	    combined latency is max(asr_time, diarization_time) rather than the sum.
308	    """
309	    if diarization is not None and executor is not None:
310	        asr_future = executor.submit(_run_asr, recognizer, samples, sample_rate)
311	        diar_future = executor.submit(diarization.process, samples)
312	        text = asr_future.result()
313	        diar_result = diar_future.result()
314	        speaker_id: Optional[int] = _dominant_speaker(diar_result) if text else None
315	    else:
316	        text = _run_asr(recognizer, samples, sample_rate)
317	        speaker_id = None
318	
319	    if text:
320	        sys.stdout.write(f"\r{' ' * 20}\r")
321	        sys.stdout.flush()
322	        _rich_print(text, speaker_id, show_speaker_tag=show_speaker_tag)

460	def _safe_extract_tar(tar: tarfile.TarFile, path: Path) -> None:
461	    """Safely extract tar contents to `path`, preventing path traversal and links.
462	
463	    This emulates the behavior of `filter="data"` available in Python 3.12+,
464	    but is compatible with Python 3.8+.
465	    """
466	    base_path = path.resolve()
467	    for member in tar.getmembers():
468	        # Skip symlinks and hard links for safety.
469	        if member.issym() or member.islnk():
470	            continue
471	
472	        member_path = (base_path / member.name).resolve()
473	        try:
474	            # Ensure the target path is within the intended base directory.
475	            member_path.relative_to(base_path)
476	        except ValueError:
477	            # Path traversal attempt or otherwise outside base directory; skip.
478	            continue
479	
480	        tar.extract(member, path=base_path)

14	# ── Rich console (no markup auto-escaping needed; we build Text objects) ────

18	def _is_dark_terminal() -> bool:
19	    """Detect whether the terminal has a dark background.
20	
21	    Primary signal: the COLORFGBG environment variable (set by many
22	    xterm-compatible terminals). Its format is ``foreground;background`` where
23	    the background field is a standard ANSI colour index:
24	
25	    +---------+-------------------------------------------+-----------+
26	    | Index   | Colour                                    | BG type   |
27	    +=========+===========================================+===========+
28	    | 0–6     | black, red, green, yellow, blue,          | dark      |
29	    |         | magenta, cyan                             |           |
30	    +---------+-------------------------------------------+-----------+
31	    | 7       | white / light-grey                        | light     |
32	    +---------+-------------------------------------------+-----------+
33	    | 8–15    | bright variants (bright-black … white)    | light     |
34	    +---------+-------------------------------------------+-----------+
35	
36	    Falls back to ``True`` (dark) when the signal is absent — dark backgrounds
37	    are the common default in developer environments.
38	    """
39	    colorfgbg = os.environ.get("COLORFGBG", "")
40	    if colorfgbg:
41	        try:
42	            bg = int(colorfgbg.split(";")[-1])
43	            # Indices 0-6: standard dark colours (black … cyan) → dark bg.
44	            # Index 7 (white) and 8-15 (bright variants) → treat as light.
45	            return bg <= 6
46	        except (ValueError, IndexError):
47	            pass
48	    return True  # Safe default: most developer terminals use a dark background.
49	
50	
51	# ── Speaker colour palettes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
52	# Dark-background palette: bright/saturated colours contrast well against dark.
53	_DARK_SPEAKER_COLOURS = [
54	    "bright_cyan",
55	    "bright_magenta",
56	    "bright_yellow",
57	    "bright_green",
58	    "bright_blue",
59	    "bright_red",
60	    "cyan",
61	    "magenta",
62	    "yellow",
63	    "green",
64	]
65	
66	# Light-background palette: darker/richer shades that contrast against white.
67	_LIGHT_SPEAKER_COLOURS = [
68	    "dark_cyan",
69	    "dark_magenta",
70	    "dark_green",
71	    "blue",
72	    "red",
73	    "dark_orange",
74	    "dark_violet",
75	    "dark_goldenrod",
76	    "teal",
77	    "purple",
78	]
79	
80	# Palette chosen once at import time based on the detected terminal background.
81	_SPEAKER_COLOURS = _DARK_SPEAKER_COLOURS if _is_dark_terminal() else _LIGHT_SPEAKER_COLOURS
82	
83	_PREFIX = "  "

85	
86	def _speaker_colour(speaker_id: int) -> str:
87	    return _SPEAKER_COLOURS[speaker_id % len(_SPEAKER_COLOURS)]
88	
89	
90	def _rich_print(
91	    text: str,
92	    speaker_id: Optional[int] = None,
93	    show_speaker_tag: bool = False,
94	) -> None:
95	    """Print a finalised line, optionally coloured (and tagged) by speaker.
96	
97	    When *speaker_id* is set, the text is coloured with that speaker's colour.
98	    The ``[Speaker N]`` label prefix is only shown when *show_speaker_tag* is
99	    ``True`` (default: colour-only, no tag).
100	    """
101	    if speaker_id is not None:
102	        colour = _speaker_colour(speaker_id)
103	        t = Text()
104	        if show_speaker_tag:
105	            t.append(f"{_PREFIX}[Speaker {speaker_id}] ", style=f"bold {colour}")
106	            t.append(text, style=colour)
107	        else:
108	            t.append(f"{_PREFIX}{text}", style=colour)
109	        _console.print(t)
110	    else:
111	        _console.print(f"{_PREFIX}{text}")
112	
113	
114	def _dominant_speaker(result: sherpa_onnx.OfflineSpeakerDiarizationResult) -> int:
115	    """Return the speaker id that covers the most time in this segment."""
116	    segments = result.sort_by_start_time()
117	    if not segments:
118	        return 0
119	    duration: dict[int, float] = {}
120	    for seg in segments:
121	        duration[seg.speaker] = duration.get(seg.speaker, 0.0) + (seg.end - seg.start)
122	    return max(duration, key=duration.__getitem__)
123	
124	
125	# ── Online (streaming) recogniser loop ──────────────────────────────────────
126	
127	def run_streaming(
128	    recognizer: sherpa_onnx.OnlineRecognizer,
129	    audio_gen: Generator[np.ndarray, None, None],
130	    sample_rate: int = 16000,
131	    show_mic_level: bool = False,
132	    diarization: Optional[sherpa_onnx.OfflineSpeakerDiarization] = None,
133	    show_speaker_tag: bool = False,
134	) -> None:
135	    """Feed incremental audio chunks into the recognizer and render output.
136	
137	    Display strategy:
138	      - Partial hypotheses: overwrite the current terminal line with \\r
139	        (near-zero latency feedback, avoids line spam).
140	      - Finalized segments: printed on a new line when an endpoint is detected.
141	
142	    When *diarization* is provided the accumulated audio for each utterance is
143	    sent to the diarization pipeline in a background thread so that it runs
144	    concurrently with the next ASR utterance, keeping added latency near zero.
145	    Each speaker's output is colour-coded; when *show_speaker_tag* is ``True``
146	    a ``[Speaker N]`` prefix is also printed.
147	    """
148	    stream = recognizer.create_stream()
149	    last_partial = ""
150	    # Buffer raw audio for the current utterance (used for diarization).
151	    audio_buf: list[np.ndarray] = []
152	    executor: Optional[ThreadPoolExecutor] = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1) if diarization is not None else None
153	    pending: Optional[Future] = None  # diarization future for the *previous* utterance
154	
155	    def _submit_diarization(samples: np.ndarray) -> Optional[Future]:
156	        if executor is None or diarization is None:
157	            return None
158	        return executor.submit(diarization.process, samples)
159	
160	    def _flush_pending(pending_future: Optional[Future], pending_text: str) -> None:
161	        """Print the pending utterance with its diarization label (if available)."""
162	        if not pending_text:
163	            return
164	        speaker_id = None
165	        if pending_future is not None and pending_future.done():
166	            try:
167	                result = pending_future.result()
168	                speaker_id = _dominant_speaker(result)
169	            except Exception as exc:
170	                logging.debug(
171	                    "Diarization failed for utterance %r: %s",
172	                    pending_text,
173	                    exc,
174	                    exc_info=True,
175	                )
176	        _rich_print(pending_text, speaker_id, show_speaker_tag=show_speaker_tag)
177	
178	    pending_text = ""
179	
180	    try:
181	        for chunk in audio_gen:
182	            stream.accept_waveform(sample_rate, chunk)
183	            if diarization is not None:
184	                audio_buf.append(chunk)
185	
186	            # Decode all queued frames immediately
187	            while recognizer.is_ready(stream):
188	                recognizer.decode_stream(stream)
189	
190	            text = recognizer.get_result(stream).strip()
191	
192	            if show_mic_level and not text:
193	                energy = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(chunk ** 2)))
194	                bar = "█" * min(int(energy * 500), 40)
195	                sys.stdout.write(f"\r{_PREFIX}mic: {bar:<40} {energy:.4f}")
196	                sys.stdout.flush()
197	
198	            if recognizer.is_endpoint(stream):
199	                if text:
200	                    if show_mic_level:
201	                        try:
202	                            width = shutil.get_terminal_size(fallback=(80, 20)).columns
203	                        except OSError:
204	                            width = 80
205	                        sys.stdout.write("\r" + " " * width + "\r")
206	                        sys.stdout.flush()
207	                    _clear_line(last_partial)
208	                    # Flush the previous utterance (diarization may now be done).
209	                    _flush_pending(pending, pending_text)
210	                    # Submit diarization for this utterance, but avoid queueing
211	                    # multiple diarization tasks when using a single worker.
212	                    if diarization is not None and audio_buf:
213	                        seg_audio = np.concatenate(audio_buf)
214	                        if pending is None or pending.done():
215	                            pending = _submit_diarization(seg_audio)
216	                            pending_text = text
217	                        else:
218	                            # Diarization worker is still busy; skip diarization
219	                            # for this utterance and flush plain text immediately.
220	                            _flush_pending(None, text)
221	                            pending_text = ""
222	                    else:
223	                        pending = None
224	                        pending_text = text
225	                        _flush_pending(None, pending_text)
226	                        pending_text = ""
227	                recognizer.reset(stream)
228	                audio_buf.clear()
229	                last_partial = ""
230	            elif text != last_partial:
231	                sys.stdout.write(f"\r{_PREFIX}{text}")
232	                sys.stdout.flush()
233	                last_partial = text
234	
235	    except KeyboardInterrupt:
236	        pass
237	    finally:
238	        _flush_tail(recognizer, stream, sample_rate, last_partial)
239	        # Flush the last pending diarization result.
240	        _flush_pending(pending, pending_text)
241	        if executor is not None:
242	            executor.shutdown(wait=True)
243	
244	
245	# ── Offline VAD-segmented loop ───────────────────────────────────────────────
246	
247	def run_offline_vad_streaming(
248	    recognizer: sherpa_onnx.OfflineRecognizer,
249	    vad: sherpa_onnx.VoiceActivityDetector,
250	    audio_gen: Generator[np.ndarray, None, None],
251	    sample_rate: int = 48000,
252	    show_mic_level: bool = False,
253	    diarization: Optional[sherpa_onnx.OfflineSpeakerDiarization] = None,
254	    show_speaker_tag: bool = False,
255	) -> None:
256	    """VAD-segmented offline ASR with optional concurrent speaker diarization.
257	
258	    For each speech segment the ASR and diarization models run concurrently
259	    in a ThreadPoolExecutor so that neither doubles the per-segment latency.
260	    Each speaker's output is colour-coded; when *show_speaker_tag* is ``True``
261	    a ``[Speaker N]`` prefix is also printed.
262	    """
263	    executor: Optional[ThreadPoolExecutor] = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) if diarization else None
264	
265	    try:
266	        for chunk in audio_gen:
267	            vad.accept_waveform(chunk)
268	
269	            if show_mic_level:
270	                energy = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(chunk ** 2)))
271	                bar = "█" * min(int(energy * 500), 40)
272	                sys.stdout.write(f"\r{_PREFIX}mic: {bar:<40} {energy:.4f}")
273	                sys.stdout.flush()
274	
275	            while not vad.empty():
276	                segment = vad.front
277	                samples = np.array(segment.samples, dtype=np.float32)
278	                vad.pop()
279	                _decode_and_print(recognizer, samples, sample_rate, diarization, executor, show_speaker_tag)
280	
281	    except KeyboardInterrupt:
282	        pass
283	    finally:
284	        vad.flush()
285	        while not vad.empty():
286	            segment = vad.front
287	            samples = np.array(segment.samples, dtype=np.float32)
288	            vad.pop()
289	            _decode_and_print(recognizer, samples, sample_rate, diarization, executor, show_speaker_tag)
290	        sys.stdout.write("\n")
291	        sys.stdout.flush()
292	        if executor is not None:
293	            executor.shutdown(wait=True)
294	
295	
296	def _decode_and_print(
297	    recognizer: sherpa_onnx.OfflineRecognizer,
298	    samples: np.ndarray,
299	    sample_rate: int,
300	    diarization: Optional[sherpa_onnx.OfflineSpeakerDiarization] = None,
301	    executor: Optional[ThreadPoolExecutor] = None,
302	    show_speaker_tag: bool = False,
303	) -> None:
304	    """Run ASR (and optionally diarization) on *samples* and print the result.
305	
306	    ASR and diarization are submitted concurrently to *executor* so that the
307	    combined latency is max(asr_time, diarization_time) rather than the sum.
308	    """
309	    if diarization is not None and executor is not None:
310	        asr_future = executor.submit(_run_asr, recognizer, samples, sample_rate)
311	        diar_future = executor.submit(diarization.process, samples)
312	        text = asr_future.result()
313	        diar_result = diar_future.result()
314	        speaker_id: Optional[int] = _dominant_speaker(diar_result) if text else None
315	    else:
316	        text = _run_asr(recognizer, samples, sample_rate)
317	        speaker_id = None
318	
319	    if text:
320	        sys.stdout.write(f"\r{' ' * 20}\r")
321	        sys.stdout.flush()
322	        _rich_print(text, speaker_id, show_speaker_tag=show_speaker_tag)
323	
324	
325	def _run_asr(
326	    recognizer: sherpa_onnx.OfflineRecognizer,
327	    samples: np.ndarray,
328	    sample_rate: int,
329	) -> str:
330	    stream = recognizer.create_stream()
331	    stream.accept_waveform(sample_rate, samples)
332	    recognizer.decode_stream(stream)
333	    return stream.result.text.strip()
334	
335	
336	def _clear_line(partial: str) -> None:
337	    """Overwrite the partial hypothesis line with spaces to prevent leftover text."""
338	    if partial:
339	        width = len(_PREFIX) + len(partial)
340	        sys.stdout.write(f"\r{' ' * width}\r")
341	        sys.stdout.flush()
342	
343	
344	def _flush_tail(
345	    recognizer: sherpa_onnx.OnlineRecognizer,
346	    stream: sherpa_onnx.OnlineStream,
347	    sample_rate: int,
348	    last_partial: str,
349	) -> None:
350	    """Flush any audio left in the recognizer pipeline after the loop ends."""
351	    tail = np.zeros(int(sample_rate * 0.5), dtype=np.float32)
352	    stream.accept_waveform(sample_rate, tail)
353	    while recognizer.is_ready(stream):
354	        recognizer.decode_stream(stream)
355	    text = recognizer.get_result(stream).strip()
356	    if text:
357	        _clear_line(last_partial)
358	        _console.print(f"{_PREFIX}{text}")
359	    sys.stdout.write("\n")
360	    sys.stdout.flush()
361

314	def _run_download_model(tmp_path, model_dir_name: str, model_type: str):
315	    """Helper: run _download_model with mocked I/O, return the URL passed to _download_file."""
316	    model_dir = tmp_path / model_dir_name
317	    # Create the extracted directory so the rename step succeeds
318	    extracted_name = _extracted_name_for(model_dir_name, model_type)
319	    extracted_dir = tmp_path / extracted_name
320	    extracted_dir.mkdir()
321	
322	    captured_url = {}
323	
324	    def fake_download(url, dest):
325	        captured_url["url"] = url
326	
327	    with patch.object(main_module, "_download_file", side_effect=fake_download), \
328	         patch("tarfile.open") as mock_tar:
329	        mock_tar.return_value.__enter__ = MagicMock(return_value=MagicMock())
330	        mock_tar.return_value.__exit__ = MagicMock(return_value=False)
331	        main_module._download_model(str(model_dir), model_type)
332	
333	    return captured_url["url"]
334	
335	
336	def _extracted_name_for(model_dir_name: str, model_type: str) -> str:
337	    if model_type == "ja" or model_dir_name == main_module._REAZON_JA_TARGET:
338	        return main_module._REAZON_JA_EXTRACTED
339	    if model_type in ("ja-en", "ja-en-mls-5k") or model_dir_name in (
340	        main_module._REAZON_JA_EN_TARGET,
341	        main_module._REAZON_JA_EN_MLS_TARGET,
342	    ):
343	        return main_module._REAZON_JA_EN_EXTRACTED
344	    if model_type == "nemo_transducer" or model_dir_name in (
345	        main_module._PARAKEET_FP16_TARGET,
346	        main_module._PARAKEET_INT8_TARGET,
347	    ):
348	        if "int8" in model_dir_name:
349	            return main_module._PARAKEET_INT8_EXTRACTED
350	        return main_module._PARAKEET_FP16_EXTRACTED
351	    return main_module._MODEL_EXTRACTED
352

333	    def _progress(block: int, block_size: int, total: int) -> None:
334	        if total > 0:
335	            pct = min(100, block * block_size * 100 // total)
336	            sys.stdout.write(f"\r  {pct}%")
337	            sys.stdout.flush()
338

346	def _safe_tar_members(tf: tarfile.TarFile, dest_dir: Path):
347	    """Yield only safe members for extraction into dest_dir.
348	
349	    This emulates the safety guarantees of `filter="data"` on Python < 3.12:
350	    - prevent path traversal (no entries may escape dest_dir)
351	    - skip device files
352	    """
353	    dest_dir_resolved = dest_dir.resolve()
354	    for member in tf.getmembers():
355	        # Skip device files and other special devices
356	        if member.isdev():
357	            continue
358	
359	        member_path = (dest_dir / member.name).resolve()
360	        try:
361	            member_path.relative_to(dest_dir_resolved)
362	        except ValueError:
363	            # This member would escape dest_dir (e.g., via .. or absolute path)
364	            continue
365	
366	        yield member

11	def _require_soundfile():
12	    global sf
13	    if getattr(sf, "SoundFile", None) is not None:
14	        return sf
15	    try:
16	        import soundfile as _soundfile  # noqa: PLC0415

26	def _require_sounddevice():
27	    global sd
28	    if getattr(sd, "InputStream", None) is not None:
29	        return sd
30	    try:
31	        import sounddevice as _sounddevice  # noqa: PLC0415
32	    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - depends on environment
33	        raise RuntimeError(
34	            "sounddevice is required for microphone input. "
35	            "Install it with: pip install sounddevice"
36	        ) from exc
37	    sd = _sounddevice
38	    return sd

41	def read_wav(
42	    path: str,
43	    target_sr: int = 16000,
44	    chunk_size: float = 0.16,
45	) -> Generator[np.ndarray, None, None]:
46	    """Read a mono audio file (WAV, FLAC, etc.) and yield float32 chunks."""
47	    sf = _require_soundfile()
48	    with sf.SoundFile(path) as f:
49	        if f.channels != 1:
50	            raise ValueError(
51	                f"Expected mono audio, got {f.channels} channels. "
52	                f"Re-sample with: ffmpeg -i <in> -ar {target_sr} -ac 1 out.wav"
53	            )
54	        if f.samplerate != target_sr:
55	            raise ValueError(
56	                f"Expected {target_sr} Hz audio, got {f.samplerate} Hz. "
57	                f"Re-sample with: ffmpeg -i <in> -ar {target_sr} -ac 1 out.wav"
58	            )
59	        chunk_frames = int(target_sr * chunk_size)
60	        while True:
61	            samples = f.read(chunk_frames, dtype="float32")
62	            if len(samples) == 0:
63	                break
64	            yield samples
65	
66	
67	def mic_stream(
68	    capture_rate: int = 16000,
69	    chunk_size: float = 0.1,
70	) -> Generator[np.ndarray, None, None]:
71	    """Capture microphone audio and yield float32 chunks via a queue.
72	
73	    capture_rate: sample rate for the microphone (default 16 kHz).
74	    Use 48000 for better compatibility with system microphones that prefer
75	    48/44.1 kHz — sherpa-onnx resamples to the model rate internally.
76	
77	    Uses a callback-based InputStream so audio capture never blocks the
78	    decoding loop — chunks are queued and consumed independently.
79	    """
80	    sd = _require_sounddevice()
81	    chunk_frames = int(capture_rate * chunk_size)
82	    q: queue.Queue[np.ndarray] = queue.Queue()
83	
84	    def _callback(
85	        indata: np.ndarray, frames: int, time, status  # noqa: ANN001
86	    ) -> None:
87	        if status:
88	            print(f"[audio] {status}", flush=True)
89	        # indata shape: (frames, 1) — flatten to 1-D
90	        q.put(indata[:, 0].copy())
91	
92	    with sd.InputStream(
93	        samplerate=capture_rate,
94	        channels=1,
95	        dtype="float32",
96	        blocksize=chunk_frames,
97	        callback=_callback,
98	    ):
99	        while True:
100	            yield q.get()
101

class TestMicStreamStatus:
    def test_status_printed_when_nonzero(self, capsys):
        import sherox.audio as audio_module
        mock_stream_ctx = MagicMock()
        mock_stream_ctx.__enter__ = MagicMock(return_value=mock_stream_ctx)
        mock_stream_ctx.__exit__ = MagicMock(return_value=False)

        callback_ref = {}

        def fake_input_stream(**kwargs):
            callback_ref["cb"] = kwargs["callback"]
            # Put something so next() returns
            indata = MagicMock()
            indata.__getitem__ = MagicMock(return_value=MagicMock(copy=MagicMock(return_value=MagicMock())))
            kwargs["callback"](
                __import__("numpy").ones((1600, 1), dtype="float32"),
                1600, None, None
            )
            return mock_stream_ctx

        with patch("sherox.audio.sd.InputStream", side_effect=fake_input_stream):
            next(audio_module.mic_stream())

        # Now call the callback again with a status
        import numpy as np
        indata = np.ones((1600, 1), dtype="float32")
        callback_ref["cb"](indata, 1600, None, "input overflow")
        out = capsys.readouterr().out
        assert "input overflow" in out
